name: addpipe24_full_flat_cla
rationale: Across our own attempts, unstaged/flat sum-of-products carry expressions consistently beat explicitly staged prefix-tree constructions at the same partition granularity (cla_block4 flat SOP: WNS 7.436 beat cla_block4_kstree staged: 7.389; cla_block3_flat: 7.390 beat cla_block3_kstree: 7.353). This suggests forcing an artificial multi-level hierarchy (via named per-stage wires) prevents ABC from finding its own optimal balanced gate network, whereas flat boolean expressions let the optimizer freely rebalance. All previous flat attempts still imposed an artificial block-partition boundary (grouping bits into blocks with a separate block-G/P layer). This candidate removes that boundary entirely: it implements the full 24-bit carry-lookahead recurrence c_i = OR_k[ g_k AND (AND_{m=k+1..i-1} p_m) ] directly via Verilog reduction operators (&, |) over generate-computed constant slices, with no manual staging at all. Reduction operators over static ranges synthesize as balanced multi-input trees by default, giving ABC a single flat boolean network to optimize globally (much like how the native tool-inferred '+' achieves the best measured WNS so far), while avoiding the extra block-boundary logic level that all our partitioned hybrid designs paid for. This is a structurally new experiment (no staged G/P propagation, no fixed radix, no block partition) that could close the residual WNS gap to the baseline while possibly costing less area than full Kogge-Stone (549.8) due to natural term sharing during synthesis.
